_doc: What gpu-validate.ps1 (the Windows battery) expects of each step, per graphics card. The battery
judges its own bundle against this file and exits 0 when every step it ran did what is declared
here, 2 when one did not (each named in summary.txt), and 3 when this file cannot be read. Steps
a -Quick run skips are not judged. Before this file the battery always exited 0 and summary.txt
explained the reds away in prose (design/live-render-robustness.md 7.8).
A card is found by its adapter slug: the adapter line's name, lowercase, every run of other
characters one '-' ("AMD Radeon RX 6800 XT" -> "amd-radeon-rx-6800-xt"; the app's calibration::slug).
A card's entry overrides 'default' step by step. Per step:
exit         the exit codes that are expected; any other is a failure of the battery.
known_fails  (optional) when the step exits non-zero, every '[FAIL] <name>' line in its output
must start with one of these; a failing check not listed is a NEW failure.
why          the reason, for the reader of summary.txt.
A card that newly PASSES a step expected to fail is also reported: the file is then stale.

build-id.why: the binary under test is the one the share published

gputest.why: exit 1 = this stack's compiler folds the df32 error-free transforms; the app detects the capability, and the rows are the data

selftest.why: goldens are compared cross-GPU off the reference card, so a failure is a real signal

live-res.why: must pass everywhere: a card without TIMESTAMP_QUERY still settles at native resolution

bench-matrix.why: 2 = algorithmic drift on a card whose own baseline exists

livetest.why: live view vs offline render on this machine; 2 = drift or a FAIL/STARVED checkpoint

uitest.why: the deep floatexp band is WARN-not-FAIL by design

recordtest.why: must pass everywhere: the frame record diagnoses the next crash

screen.why: 0 = three dives captured; the verdict is screengate.py's

gputest.why: every NVIDIA backend folds the transforms (measured)
the RX 6800 XT folds them on every backend under Windows (measured)

known_fails: a wider canvas contains the narrower one
selftest.why: known: under Windows a few texels at 1e2x differ between a wide and a narrow canvas (under Linux it is floatexp vs df32 instead, which this Windows battery never sees)
